history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 421 / Ayyappa Temple — that earlier file describes the same Sector 5 Bokaro Steel City Ayyappa temple (same 11 July 1983 date, same Ayyappa Seva Sangham management, matching coordinates); dedup candidate. A South-Indian-style Ayyappa temple in Sector 5, Bokaro Steel City (administrative office: Sector V; beside Chinmaya Vidyalaya), established 11 July 1983 for the large Tamil/Malayali community of the steel township — a visitor review notes it was founded by Bokaro's Tamil community and stands on about 2 acres of land. The sanctum holds Lord Ayyappa, with additional shrines for Ganesha, Kartikeya, Goddess Bhagavati and Rama & Sita; one travel source describes the architecture as resembling 'quintessential Bengali architecture' (UNVERIFIED — architectural description from a single weak source). The shrine is managed by the Ayyappa Seva Sangham Bokaro Steel City; reviews describe a calm, clean, well-maintained complex with prasad served on Saturdays and Sundays. The official temple website is ayyappatemplebokaro.in (cited by a place directory; not independently verified).

name: Sri Ayyappa Temple
town_description: Bokaro Steel City is a planned industrial city in Bokaro district, Jharkhand, built around the Bokaro Steel Plant — one of India's first public-sector steel plants, commissioned in the 1960s with Soviet collaboration. The city is laid out in numbered sectors with broad avenues, parks and markets, and draws settlers from across India, which is reflected in its temples representing many regional traditions. Nearby attractions include Garga Dam, the Parasnath Hills (a major Jain pilgrimage site) and the Rajrappa Chhinnamasta temple.
